scenarios.title: Delete, reload, then restore without the reload workaround
scenarios.expected: Canonical/recovery state is removed, stale tabs cannot resurrect it, EVT is preserved, actual backup restores and can save.
scenarios.observed: Deletion removed the canonical, verified, migration and legacy records. Restore Stored Data and a stale tab did not resurrect them; EVT data was unchanged. After reloading the empty app, direct reimport of the downloaded backup failed with the same revision mismatch as COLD01. DZ04 subsequently restored that exact backup using the tested reload workaround and saved another change.
scenarios.notes: One composite scenario: the deletion/isolation assertions passed; the final direct recovery assertion failed. This is the same underlying defect as COLD01, not a second independent defect.

findings.title: First import fails in a fresh profile or after deleted-workspace reload
findings.status: Fixed locally; public build not updated
findings.expected: Opening Settings and applying a valid workspace should succeed without a browser reload.
findings.observed: Settings navigation writes durable revision 1 while in-memory revision stays 0. Apply import fails with “Workspace changed before this mutation could be committed. Reload and retry.” The same failure was reproduced after permanent deletion and reload.
steps: Open the published NSA URL in a clean browser profile.
Choose the area-pricing v5 JSON and click Apply import.
Observe the dialog remains open and Save failed appears.
Reload the page, reopen Settings and import the same file: it succeeds.
findings.impact: Blocks a smooth first-use import or recovery demonstration. No loss of the source file or downloaded backup was observed.
findings.workaround: Open Settings, reload the page, then select and apply the JSON. Verified in Chromium and Edge. This is an operational workaround, not a fix.
findings.recommendation: Obtain separate publication authorization, verify deployed source, then repeat immediate import, deletion/recovery and the headed demonstration.

findings.title: Converted workspace has 57 data-health warnings
findings.expected: Make inherited data limitations visible before the demonstration.
findings.observed: 0 relationship errors; 54 legacy-catalog warnings, 2 missing Council Operational Amount warnings and 1 pending status-migration readiness review.
steps: Import the converted file using the verified workaround.
Open Data and Settings and click Run checks.
findings.impact: Do not present status automation as enabled or Council operational funding as already configured. These are inherited data warnings, not failed financial arithmetic.
findings.workaround: Use the customer-funded rehearsal path unless the relevant configuration is explicitly reviewed and updated.
findings.recommendation: Review migration readiness and the two Council funding amounts before demonstrating those behaviours.

findings.title: Import preview does not display entity counts
findings.expected: The testing plan called for checking counts in the preview.
findings.observed: The preview shows a signature-inspection message and Apply/Cancel controls, but not the 12 / 2 / 50 / 54 entity counts. Counts were verified after applying and against the input independently.
steps: Choose the converted JSON in Settings.
Inspect the staged import dialog before applying.
findings.impact: The operator cannot reconcile entity counts from the preview itself.
findings.workaround: Use the report baseline and post-import record checks.
findings.recommendation: Consider count visibility separately; this report does not introduce a UI change.

If any import or save fails, stop entering data. Keep the original file and backups, record the displayed error, reload and repeat only the verified recovery route.
demo: Launch the prepared original-data Edge profile and confirm Register totals. Do not demonstrate a clean-profile first import without acknowledging the blocker.
